lines: Two mixers in one module: a four-input X mixer with a level knob on every input, and a four-input Y mixer with one knob on the sum; both are DC-coupled and mix signals between -10V and 10V
Sets the level of the summed Y inputs at the Y output, on a logarithmic taper
Sets the level of that input in the X mix, on a logarithmic taper
One of the four inputs into the X mixer
One of the four inputs into the Y mixer
An input into the Y mixer; with nothing patched here the X+ output is fed to it, which makes the Y knob a master level over X and Y together
The X mix
The X mix with its polarity inverted
The Y mix
The X mix and the Y mix added together
MAR.notes: No family is given to the signal jacks: the maker states the module is DC-coupled for audio, control voltage and gates alike, so what a jack carries is whatever is patched into it.

lines: Voltage-controlled filter on a V2164 core, with simultaneous two-pole low-pass and band-pass outputs; at high resonance it self-oscillates as a clean sine oscillator
Sets the cutoff frequency; fully clockwise the filter is wide open, and fully counter-clockwise it is shut and nothing passes
Sets the resonance, emphasising the frequencies around the cutoff; self-oscillation begins at about 80 percent of the travel
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the CVF input before it reaches the cutoff frequency
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the CVR input before it reaches the resonance
Modulates the cutoff frequency, through the CVF knob
Sets the cutoff frequency one octave per volt with no attenuation, so the filter tracks a keyboard
Modulates the resonance, through the CVR knob; about 4V here brings the filter to self-oscillation
The signal into the filter, DC-coupled
The two-pole low-pass output, falling 12dB per octave above the cutoff
The two-pole band-pass output, 12dB per octave either side of the cutoff
Four linear voltage-controlled amplifiers, cascaded left to right so that any output left unpatched is added into the next channel's output; the fourth amplifier is controlled only by its CV input
Sets the starting gain of that amplifier, which is added to the voltage at its control input; the maximum bias is 5V, which is a gain of 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at that channel's CV input before it sets the gain
The signal into that amplifier, DC-coupled so audio, control voltage and triggers all pass
Sets the gain of that amplifier, added to its gain knob; 5V opens the amplifier fully and higher voltages are clipped
Sets the gain of the fourth amplifier; with nothing patched here it is held at an internal 5V, which leaves that amplifier fully open
The output of that amplifier; with no cable patched here its signal is added into the next channel's output instead
The output of the fourth amplifier, carrying the sum of it and every earlier channel whose own output is unpatched
Four attack-decay envelope generators with an exponential shape, each free-running as a looping low-frequency oscillator while its trigger input is unpatched
Sets the rise time of that channel, the climb from zero to the maximum level
Sets the fall time of that channel, the drop from the maximum level back to zero
Picks the time range for that channel: at the fastest the rise runs 0.1ms to 400ms and the fall 0.1ms to 600ms, the middle position makes both ten times longer, and the slowest a hundred times longer
A trigger or gate here fires that channel's envelope; with nothing patched the channel loops instead, the fall retriggering the rise
The envelope of that channel, 0-9V when it is triggered and 1-9V while it free-runs
QUART.notes: The three-position switch is unlabelled on the panel and the maker's tooltip calls it a frequency divider; the hardware manual calls the same control TIME RANGE with fast, medium and slow positions. The multipliers of one, ten and a hundred were read from the compiled plugin, which position on the switch is which was not settled.

lines: Analog triangle-core oscillator on a 3340 chip, with sine, triangle, saw and pulse outputs, two waves mixed with the pulse, and two sub-octave squares, all at plus and minus 5V
An eight-position switch setting the coarse pitch, each step one octave
Tunes the pitch about seven semitones either side of the centre position
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FM input before it reaches the frequency
Sets the pulse width of the pulse and the two mixed waves: 1 percent fully counter-clockwise, a square wave at 3 o'clock, 100 percent fully clockwise; a cable in the PW input makes it an attenuator
Picks whether the FM input changes the frequency linearly or exponentially
Picks the range: VCO runs from 20Hz to over 40kHz, LFO runs from cycles over a minute long up to low audio rates
Modulates the oscillator frequency, through the FM knob and in the response picked by the FM switch
Sets the pitch one octave per volt, raising it for positive voltages and lowering it for negative
A waveform of plus and minus 5V here resets the oscillator's phase, for hard sync
Modulates the pulse width of the pulse and the two mixed waves over a 0-5V range, through the PW knob
The sine output
The triangle output
The sawtooth output, the richest in harmonics of the four classic waves
The pulse output, its duty cycle set by the PW knob
A triangle wave mixed with the pulse wave, so the PW knob shapes it as well
A sawtooth wave mixed with the pulse wave, so the PW knob shapes it as well
A square wave one octave below the oscillator's pitch
A square wave two octaves below the oscillator's pitch
ONA.notes: The maker's tooltip calls the FM knob an attenuverter and the hardware manual calls it an attenuator; the tooltip was followed. The maker's tooltips name the two mixed outputs Morph 1 and Morph 2, and the hardware manual calls the same two Complex 1 and Complex 2.

lines: ADSR envelope generator with a slider and a control voltage input for each stage, and a separate signal path through an attenuverter and an offset

Sets the decay time, the fall from the maximum level to the sustain level

lines: Expander for the Performance Mixer, placed immediately to its left, adding a stereo direct output and a mute gate input for each channel, and an aux control voltage input for each stereo channel
The left side of that channel of the mixer, taken after its fader
The right side of that channel of the mixer, taken after its fader

EXP4.notes: The side the expander goes on, and the 2V mute threshold, were read from the compiled plugin: the mixer looks to its left for the expander and the expander looks to its right for the mixer.

lines: Random voltage generator with an internal clock, a probability control, and the same random value shaped four ways at four outputs; it is the hardware version of the VCV Random module
Sets the tempo of the internal clock
Sets the chance of a new random value being generated on each clock tick
Blends the previous value with a new random one, which sets how far the output moves each time
Sets the shape of the transition to each new value at all four shaped outputs
Picks the range of the shaped outputs: unipolar 0-10V with the switch up, bipolar -5V to 5V with it down
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at that parameter's control voltage input before it is added to the slider
Modulates the clock tempo, through the RATE attenuverter
Modulates the chance of a new value, through the PROB attenuverter
Modulates the blend between the old and the new value, through the RND attenuverter
Modulates the transition shape, through the SHAPE attenuverter
A trigger here clocks the module in place of the RATE slider, and the PROB slider sets the chance of a new value on each of those triggers
The voltage here is sampled in place of a random one at each clock, and the RND slider has no effect
A pulse each time a new random value is generated
Jumps to each new value in one step at 0 percent SHAPE, and divides the move into sixteen steps at 100 percent
Reaches each new value at once at 0 percent SHAPE, and takes the whole clock cycle to get there at 100 percent, holding steady in between
Moves to each new value along an exponential curve, at a pace set by the SHAPE slider, and becomes a straight line at 100 percent
Moves smoothly to each new value at a speed set by the SHAPE slider, then holds it until the cycle ends
Menu — Normalize OUT to CV INs feeds the LIN output back into all four control voltage inputs, so the attenuverters set how far the module modulates itself
VCVRANDOM.notes: Parameter 9 has no name and no place on the panel; it carries the menu option and no line is tagged to it.

Sets the fall time of that channel, slower turned clockwise
Sets the curve of that channel's fall, from exponential through linear at the centre to logarithmic

Sets the timing range of that channel's rise and fall: LOW for very slow modulation, MID for ordinary envelope times, HIGH for snappy percussive ones
Turned on, that channel repeats its cycle with no trigger, which makes it an oscillator
Turned on, that channel holds at its peak while the gate is high and falls once the gate is released; turned off it falls as soon as it reaches the peak

Modulates the fall time of that channel

Sets that channel's attenuverter: 0V leaves the amplitude and polarity alone, -5V inverts at full amplitude and 5V passes at full amplitude
Carries a high gate while that channel is rising
That channel's function output, after its attenuverter and its offset
Carries a high gate while that channel is falling
Goes high whenever the X channel is at a higher voltage than the Y channel
The X and Y channels added together
Whichever of the X and Y channels is at the higher voltage
Whichever of the X and Y channels is at the lower voltage
ARC.notes: The two signal inputs into the slew limiters take audio or control voltage alike, so no family is given to them.

lines: Four analog drum voices in the 808 tradition — kick, snare, closed hat and open hat — each with its own trigger, level control voltage and output, summed through a compressor and a tilt equaliser

Sets how long the snare rings on
Sets the tone of both hat voices
Sets the decay length of the hat voices
Compresses the mix: fully clockwise gives a ratio of five to one at a -10dB threshold with 22dB of makeup gain, and fully counter-clockwise leaves the mix uncompressed
Tilts the balance of the mix between low and high frequencies, and leaves it flat at the centre
A trigger here fires the kick
A trigger here fires the snare
A trigger here fires the closed hat
A trigger here fires the open hat

The kick on its own

OCTA.notes: This module has no manual. The voices are built on the daisysp analog drum models, and the ranges quoted for the kick, the snare and the compressor were read from the compiled plugin. The knob the panel labels NOISE sets the decay of the snare in the code, while SNAP sets the balance of noise against the body; the maker names them Snare Noise and Snare Snap. The sidechain output is the mix passed through a slew limiter.
